title: Microsoft Purview: DLP and auto-labeling policies for non-Microsoft connected apps
summary: The auto-labeling navigation path omits intermediate wizard headings and shortens the documented locations heading, so it needs correction before publication. The rollout dates, licensing and meter information, retirement dates, and warning about conflicting migration instructions are supported.

claims.claim: Purview is adding dedicated DLP application locations for supported non-Microsoft applications.
claims.quote: After rollout, dedicated application locations will be available in Microsoft Purview for supported non-Microsoft applications.

claims.claim: Administrators will be able to create and manage auto-labeling policies for supported non-Microsoft applications in Purview.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to create and manage DLP and auto-labeling policies directly in Microsoft Purview for supported non-Microsoft applications.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the supported conditions and actions vary by application.
claims.quote: The conditions and actions supported for each of these applications vary.

The current path omits the label-dialog and admin-unit headings and renames the final heading.

claims.claim: A dedicated non-Microsoft auto-labeling automation route is not documented, and New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy documents no parameter for these application locations.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview non-Microsoft connected apps dedicated DLP auto-labeling PowerShell New-DlpCompliancePolicy New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy locations. Opened the auto-labeling feature page and New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy reference; its Locations description is an unfilled placeholder.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-autosensitivitylabelpolicy?view=exchange-ps to sources for the reference-page absence asserted in Governance controls.

claims.claim: The retiring Instances path is Purview Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Admin units > Locations > Instances > Edit > Specific instances > + Include instances.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation All for all connected applications in the documented legacy experience.
claims.quote: The ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation parameter specifies the non-Microsoft cloud apps to include in the DLP policy. You can use the value All to include all connected apps.

claims.claim: The shown ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation command requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator membership.
claims.quote: **Note**: This parameter requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Applications have their own connector guides and enablement processes.
claims.quote: For detailed instructions, see the [app connector guides](protect-connected-apps) for each app.

claims.claim: The cited Defender for Cloud Apps Microsoft Graph page covers discovered applications.
claims.quote: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps supports a Microsoft Graph API that you can use to work with discovered cloud apps, to customize and automate the **Discovered apps** page functionality in the Microsoft Defender portal.

claims.claim: Creating equivalent policies in Purview does not remove original Defender for Cloud Apps file policies.
claims.quote: No. Migration creates new equivalent policies in Purview. Review your source and target policies in the Purview portal before you decommission any original policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[3].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: MC1449180 says to turn off or delete overlapping Defender for Cloud Apps file policies before creating the Purview policy.
claims.quote: Before you create Microsoft Purview policy for any of these non-Microsoft applications, turn off or delete any Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file policies for the same non-Microsoft locations.

claims.claim: Learn's migration page instead says to disable Defender policies only after validating and turning on Purview policies, creating the sequencing conflict the briefing reports.
claims.quote: Disable Defender for Cloud Apps policies only after you validate and turn on the Purview policies.

claims.claim: Activity explorer supports monitoring these connected-application policies.
claims.quote: Activity explorer supports non-Microsoft connected app policies. You can monitor DLP policy activity for your non-Microsoft apps in the same way you monitor Microsoft 365 locations.

claims.claim: DLP alerts support these connected-application policies.
claims.quote: DLP alerts are supported for non-Microsoft connected app policies. Alerts appear in the DLP alerts dashboard alongside alerts from other locations.

claims.claim: The sources do not describe an automatic change from the new dedicated policies for tenants that create no policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview non-Microsoft connected apps DLP auto-labeling default automatic rollout existing policies no admin action. Read the roadmap, MC1449180, both feature pages and migration page; policy creation is explicit, and the separate file-policy retirement is disclosed in the briefing.
